# tritonctl filesystem

Shared NFS filesystems

Alias: fs

Subcommands: profiles, create, list, show, resize, usage, attach, attachments, detach, delete

Usage: `tritonctl filesystem [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>`

## tritonctl filesystem profiles

List the profiles a filesystem can be created with

Usage: `tritonctl filesystem profiles [OPTIONS]`

## tritonctl filesystem create

Create a filesystem in the current project

Usage: `tritonctl filesystem create [OPTIONS] --size <SIZE> <NAME>`

- `<NAME>`
- `--size <SIZE>`: Size: `500G`, `1T`, or bytes; a whole number of GiB (required)
- `--fs-profile <PROFILE>`: Volume profile; see `tritonctl fs profiles` (default: general)
- `--vpc <VPC>`: The VPC to serve it into, when the project has more than one
- `--description <DESCRIPTION>`

## tritonctl filesystem list

List the filesystems of the current project

Alias: ls

Usage: `tritonctl filesystem list [OPTIONS]`

## tritonctl filesystem show

Show one filesystem

Usage: `tritonctl filesystem show [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Filesystem name, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl filesystem resize

Grow or shrink a filesystem. A shrink below what it holds is refused

Usage: `tritonctl filesystem resize [OPTIONS] --size <SIZE> <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Filesystem name, uuid, or prefix
- `--size <SIZE>`: New size: `1T`, `500G`, or bytes; a whole number of GiB (required)

## tritonctl filesystem usage

Show how many bytes a filesystem holds, as last metered

Usage: `tritonctl filesystem usage [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Filesystem name, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl filesystem attach

Attach a filesystem to an instance in its VPC. The instance mounts it at next boot, or by hand with the command `attachments` shows

Usage: `tritonctl filesystem attach [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE> <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Filesystem name, uuid, or prefix
- `--instance <INSTANCE>`: Instance name, uuid, or prefix (required)
- `--read-only`: Mount it read-only
- `--path <PATH>`: Where the guest mounts it; `/mnt/<name>` by default

## tritonctl filesystem attachments

List a filesystem's attachments and how to mount each

Usage: `tritonctl filesystem attachments [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Filesystem name, uuid, or prefix

## tritonctl filesystem detach

Detach a filesystem from an instance. The instance loses access; a mount inside the guest is left for the guest to undo

Usage: `tritonctl filesystem detach [OPTIONS] --instance <INSTANCE> <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Filesystem name, uuid, or prefix
- `--instance <INSTANCE>`: Instance name, uuid, or prefix (required)
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails

## tritonctl filesystem delete

Delete a filesystem and every file in it

Alias: rm

Usage: `tritonctl filesystem delete [OPTIONS] <ID>`

- `<ID>`: Filesystem name, uuid, or prefix
- `-n, --dry-run`: Print what would change and stop
- `-y, --yes`: Answer yes to the confirmation. The summary still prints
- `--keep-going`: Keep executing after a step fails
